The graded return is annual log growth, 12 times the mean monthly portfolio log return, log(1 + r). CAGR is exp(of that growth) minus 1, and it stays beside the log growth. Volatility, Sharpe, and max drawdown use the simple monthly returns. Results are gross of costs. Cash earns nothing.

## Decision

The book to trade is top-10 positive-vol with no probability overlay. Each month it forms five groups from the trailing 12-month return path, keeps at most ten high positive-vol names in each group, and invests only where one-month momentum is positive. The rest is cash. Its official-test annual log growth is higher than equal weight, and its Sharpe is lower. Factor models, a ten-factor cut, grid search, and the engineered recipes do not produce a forecast that beats a historical base rate. The engineering notebook's higher CAGR lines up with a volatility tilt that a model-free rule already captures.

```{python}
print(choice_text())
```

## Equal-weight log growth and CAGR

Training is January 2000–December 2009. The official test is January 2010–December 2018, 108 months. Combined compounds those monthly simple returns through December 2018. The graded annualized return is the official-test CAGR, shown with its annual log growth.

## Two non-ML books

All of these books are long-only and gross of costs. Cash earns nothing.

Equal weight gives every stock the same weight and stays fully invested.

Top 10 positive-vol and full baskets invest only in positive one-month momentum. One month is the last simple return the stock has already earned. Held names are weighted in proportion to that return. Every other dollar is cash.

Each month, stocks with a complete 12-month return path are split into five K-means groups, fit on those past returns. The groups are fit again the next month. A group whose own one-month return is not positive is left in cash, including members that were up on their own. Inside a group that was up, only members that were up receive weight.

Top 10 positive-vol makes each group smaller first. It keeps at most ten names per group, the ones with the highest positive volatility over the same twelve months. Positive volatility is the root-mean-square of the up months; down months contribute zero. Capital is then scaled to the names that remain, and the one-month rule above is applied.

Full baskets use the same five groups and the same one-month rule, with every name still in the group.

The training window here is January 2005–December 2009, because the groups need twelve months of history. The chart is the official test.

## Four model types

Logistic regression, Gaussian naive Bayes, random forest, and histogram gradient boosting. The first, third, and fourth have tunable hyperparameters. These official books use factory settings.

The models do not choose a new list of stocks. Each overlay starts from top-10 positive-vol or from full baskets and only rescales weights that are already positive.

Downside to cash multiplies each held weight by (1 − 0.5 × P(next month is down)). The reduction goes to cash.

Upside tilt multiplies a held weight by 1.5 when P(next month is up) is at least 0.60, then scales the stock weights back to that book's original stock budget. Cash stays where the momentum rule left it. The two adjustments are separate rows.

```{python}

```

## Categories, the ten-factor cut, and grid search

K nearest neighbors is an additional model type. It classifies the within-month quintile of the next return. The portfolio row equal-weights the names placed in the top quintile. A month with none of those names is cash at zero. The search is a training holdout, and the frozen 2010–2018 books stay on the four factory classifiers. The K-means books group past return paths and then apply the positive one-month rule.

The ten-factor question is whether a subset changes the book versus all twenty factors on the training years. GridSearchCV scores log loss on a training holdout. The official books were not refit with the chosen settings.


## Feature engineering

Two saved pieces sit behind this section. The completed study fits every learned transform inside chronological folds and scores January 2007–December 2009 without loading the test file. The table is the same K-means top-10 book, positive one-month momentum with residual cash, then a logistic downside haircut, for each recipe. The second table is the previously viewed notebook comparison on 2010–2018. Each month it equal-weights the 20% of names with the highest predicted probability and stays fully invested. Annual log growth in that table is log(1 + CAGR).

```{python}
print(source_note("engineering"))
display(style_table(engineering_holdout_table()))
comparison = engineering_comparison_table()
display(style_table(comparison).format({"Test AUC": "{:.3f}"}))
print(engineering_note())
```

Learned clusters, principal components, and IC weights are fit on training labels or training correlations and then frozen. A ten-column composite can still draw on all twenty source factors. ANOVA-10 is the cut that stays inside ten original factors. Unsupervised construction can overfit the choice of groups even when it does not use the return as a label. IC and Q5−Q1 spreads diagnose a factor. They are not the return of a long-only portfolio.
